findings.finding: _validate_instance_registry accepts a caller-supplied mapping when each record has five exact fields and STATUS ACTIVE. It verifies no canonical repository path, current-main blob, registry hash, issuer, attestation, revocation record, controller or cryptographic signature.
findings.impact: A sender can invent every active instance and thereby satisfy sender, recipient and reviewer tuple checks without proving that any other session, Life or Worker exists or consented.
findings.disposition: HOLD; either verify authenticated registry and actor attestations or explicitly downgrade the candidate to structural consistency only.

findings.finding: MESSAGE_SHA256 and EVENT_SHA256 are unkeyed hashes. The positive test constructs the complete sender-to-recipient-to-reviewer chain in one process and returns REVIEWED; SIGNATURE_TYPE is only an enum and no signature is verified.
findings.impact: Field equality and content integrity can be misrepresented as recipient ACK, answer or independent review authorship.
findings.disposition: HOLD; never promote the output to authenticated delivery, ACK, answer or review evidence.

findings.finding: seen_messages and seen_idempotency_keys are optional caller inputs, are replaced with empty maps when falsey and are never mutated or durably persisted. Reproduced consecutive validation calls both returned VALIDATED_CREATED while both supplied maps remained empty.
findings.impact: The stated replay-safe idempotency is not enforced across calls, processes or sessions and cannot guard any side effect.
findings.disposition: HOLD; require durable, atomic message-ID and idempotency-key reservation and consumption.

findings.finding: Only CREATED, ACKNOWLEDGED, ANSWERED and REVIEWED receive actor-specific constraints. Any active registry entry can author QUEUED and DELIVERED. A reproduced unrelated reviewer instance advanced the chain to DELIVERED.
findings.impact: The audit trail can claim transport delivery without evidence from an authorized transport or recipient.
findings.disposition: HOLD; bind each state transition to an explicit authenticated actor class and transport receipt.

findings.finding: REVIEWED rejects only the sender and recipient instance IDs. The registry permits a second instance record with the same SELF_NAME, LIFE_ID and WORKER_ID. A reproduced same-Life clone instance passed as a distinct reviewer.
findings.impact: One Life or controller can manufacture a second instance ID and bypass the claimed distinct review boundary.
findings.disposition: HOLD; independence must be proven across Life, Worker, controller and credential domains, not instance-ID inequality alone.

findings.finding: Message and event timestamps are only parsed. The validator does not require monotonic ordering, event time after message creation, maximum age, expiry or clock authority. A REVIEWED event timestamped in 2020 after 2026 events was accepted.
findings.impact: Backdated, future or reordered evidence can pass the hash-chain validator and appear chronological.
findings.disposition: HOLD; bind a trusted observation time and enforce monotonic, bounded event chronology.

findings.finding: REPLY_TO validation checks only that a string key exists in seen_messages. It does not bind the referenced message hash, correlation ID, repository, opposite sender-recipient direction, work order, expiry or reply authorization.
findings.impact: A reply can attach to an unrelated known message and create false conversational continuity.
findings.disposition: HOLD; verify a complete typed parent envelope and direction/correlation policy.

findings.finding: Current main declares both handoff and message runtime implementations NOT_STARTED and the security model says an Agent cannot self-authorize by writing JSON. The candidate changes protected protocol status and runtime claims without authenticated identity infrastructure.
findings.impact: Merging would promote a local structural prototype into protected protocol truth while its central trust dependency remains caller-controlled.
findings.disposition: Do not modify protected protocol or CURRENT authority until the trust model is implemented and approved.

findings.finding: All seven candidate paths are PR-only relative to their merge base, but the branch is 806 commits behind exact main and has no exact-head GitHub workflow run or commit status. Local tests pass 83/83.
findings.impact: Path non-overlap reduces transplant conflict but does not supply exact-head CI or validate the current repository policy boundary.
findings.disposition: Historical local test evidence only; any successor must start from exact current main on a non-codex branch and add security regressions.
